sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito rathopasthe mahārathaḥ niṣasāda mahārāja kaśmalaṃ ca jagāma ha
english: Pierced deep and shaken, that great warrior sank down upon the floor of his chariot, O great king, and fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: taṃ visaṃjñaṃ nipatitaṃ sūtaḥ saṃprekṣya saṃyuge apovāha rathenājau yamābhyām abhipīḍitam
english: Seeing him fallen senseless in the fight, hard pressed by the twin sons of Mādrī, his charioteer bore him away from the battle in the chariot.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā madreśvararathaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ parāṅmukham sarve vimanaso bhūtvā nedam astīty acintayan
english: When they saw the chariot of the lord of the Madras turned away in flight, all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra grew downcast and thought, 'All is lost.'

sanskrit: nirjitya mātulaṃ saṃkhye mādrīputrau mahārathau dadhmatur muditau śaṅkhau siṃhanādaṃ vinedatuḥ
english: Having vanquished their maternal uncle in battle, the two mighty sons of Mādrī, exultant, blew their conches and let forth a lion's roar.

sanskrit: abhidudruvatur hṛṣṭau tava sainyaṃ viśāṃ pate yathā daityacamūṃ rājann indropendrāv ivāmarau
english: Rejoicing, the two rushed upon your army, O lord of peoples, as the immortal gods Indra and Upendra would charge against the host of the Daityas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā madhyaṃ prāpte divākare śrutāyuṣam abhiprekṣya codayām āsa vājinaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then king Yudhiṣṭhira, when the sun had reached its zenith, fixed his gaze upon Śrutāyus and urged on his horses.

sanskrit: abhyadhāvat tato rājā śrutāyuṣam ariṃdamam vinighnan sāyakais tīkṣṇair navabhir nataparvabhiḥ
english: Then the king charged at Śrutāyus, that tamer of foes, striking him with nine sharp, smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: sa saṃvārya raṇe rājā preṣitān dharmasūnunā śarān sapta maheṣvāsaḥ kaunteyāya samarpayat
english: That king, a great archer, having warded off in battle the shafts sent by the son of Dharma, dispatched seven arrows at the son of Kuntī in return.

sanskrit: te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā papuḥ śoṇitam āhave asūn iva vicinvanto dehe tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Piercing his armor in the fray, they drank his blood, as if searching out the very life-breaths within the body of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavas tu bhṛśaṃ viddhas tena rājñā mahātmanā raṇe varāhakarṇena rājānaṃ hṛdi vivyadhe
english: But the son of Pāṇḍu, sorely wounded by that great-souled king, struck the king in the heart in battle with a boar-eared arrow.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena ketuṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ rathaśreṣṭho rathāt tūrṇaṃ bhūmau pārtho nyapātayat
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft Pārtha, foremost of chariot-warriors, swiftly cast down to the earth the banner of that great-souled one from his chariot.

sanskrit: ketuṃ nipatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutāyuḥ sa tu pārthivaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ viśikhais tīkṣṇai rājan vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Seeing his banner fallen, that king Śrutāyus, O monarch, pierced the son of Pāṇḍu with seven sharp, barbless arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhāt prajajvāla dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ yathā yugānte bhūtāni dhakṣyann iva hutāśanaḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, blazed up with wrath, like the fire that would consume all beings at the end of an age.

sanskrit: kruddhaṃ tu pāṇḍavaṃ dṛṣṭvā devagandharvarākṣasāḥ pravivyathur mahārāja vyākulaṃ cāpy abhūj jagat
english: Beholding the son of Pāṇḍu enraged, the gods, gandharvas, and rākṣasas trembled, O great king, and the whole world grew distraught.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ caiva bhūtānām idam āsīn manogatam trīṃl lokān adya saṃkruddho nṛpo 'yaṃ dhakṣyatīti vai
english: And this thought arose in the minds of all beings: 'This king, in his fury, will surely burn up the three worlds this day.'

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś caiva devāś ca cakruḥ svastyayanaṃ mahat lokānāṃ nṛpa śāntyarthaṃ krodhite pāṇḍave tadā
english: The seers and the gods then performed a great rite of blessing, O king, to bring peace to the worlds when the son of Pāṇḍu was thus enraged.

sanskrit: sa ca krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ sṛkkiṇī parilelihan dadhārātmavapur ghoraṃ yugāntādityasaṃnibham
english: And he, possessed by wrath, licking the corners of his mouth, bore a terrible form like the sun at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇi sainyāni tāvakāni viśāṃ pate nirāśāny abhavaṃs tatra jīvitaṃ prati bhārata
english: Then all your troops, O lord of peoples, lost there all hope of life, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: sa tu dhairyeṇa taṃ kopaṃ saṃnivārya mahāyaśāḥ śrutāyuṣaḥ praciccheda muṣṭideśe mahad dhanuḥ
english: But that king of great renown, restraining his anger by his firmness, cut asunder the great bow of Śrutāyus at the grip.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ nārācena stanāntare nirbibheda raṇe rājā sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Then, his bow severed, the king pierced him between the breasts with an iron shaft in battle, while all the army looked on.

sanskrit: satvaraṃ caraṇe rājaṃs tasya vāhān mahātmanaḥ nijaghāna śaraiḥ kṣipraṃ sūtaṃ ca sumahābalaḥ
english: Swiftly, O king, that mighty one slew with his arrows the horses of that great-souled foe, and quickly his charioteer as well.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ tu rathaṃ tyaktvā dṛṣṭvā rājñas tu pauruṣam vipradudrāva vegena śrutāyuḥ samare tadā
english: Abandoning his chariot whose steeds were slain, and seeing the prowess of the king, Śrutāyus then fled swiftly from the battle.

sanskrit: tasmiñ jite maheṣvāse dharmaputreṇa saṃyuge duryodhanabalaṃ rājan sarvam āsīt parāṅmukham
english: When that great archer was vanquished in battle by the son of Dharma, the whole army of Duryodhana, O king, turned its back in flight.

sanskrit: etat kṛtvā mahārāja dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vyāttānano yathā kālas tava sainyaṃ jaghāna ha
english: Having done this, O great king, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma, his mouth gaping like Death itself, smote your army.

sanskrit: cekitānas tu vārṣṇeyo gautamaṃ rathināṃ varam prekṣatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ chādayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Cekitāna of the Vṛṣṇi line covered Gautama, foremost of chariot-warriors, with his arrows, while all the armies looked on.

sanskrit: saṃnivārya śarāṃs tāṃs tu kṛpaḥ śāradvato yudhi cekitānaṃ raṇe yattaṃ rājan vivyādha patribhiḥ
english: But Kṛpa, the son of Śaradvat, having warded off those arrows in the fight, pierced with his feathered shafts the watchful Cekitāna in battle, O king.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena dhanuś ciccheda māriṣa sārathiṃ cāsya samare kṣiprahasto nyapātayat hayāṃś cāsyāvadhīd rājann ubhau ca pārṣṇisārathī
english: Then with another broad-headed arrow, O sire, the swift-handed one cut his bow and struck down his charioteer in battle, and he slew his horses, O king, and both his flank-drivers as well.

sanskrit: so 'vaplutya rathāt tūrṇaṃ gadāṃ jagrāha sātvataḥ sa tayā vīraghātinyā gadayā gadināṃ varaḥ gautamasya hayān hatvā sārathiṃ ca nyapātayat
english: Leaping swiftly down from his chariot, the Sātvata seized his mace; and with that hero-slaying mace, foremost of mace-wielders, he killed the horses of Gautama and struck down his charioteer.

sanskrit: bhūmiṣṭho gautamas tasya śarāṃś cikṣepa ṣoḍaśa te śarāḥ sātvataṃ bhittvā prāviśanta dharātalam
english: Gautama, standing upon the ground, hurled at him sixteen arrows; those shafts, piercing through the Sātvata, sank into the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: cekitānas tataḥ kruddhaḥ punaś cikṣepa tāṃ gadām gautamasya vadhākāṅkṣī vṛtrasyeva puraṃdaraḥ
english: Then Cekitāna, enraged, hurled that mace once more, longing to slay Gautama, as Indra the sacker of cities longed to slay Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ vimalām aśmagarbhāṃ mahāgadām śarair anekasāhasrair vārayām āsa gautamaḥ
english: That great mace, bright and stone-cored, as it came flying down, Gautama warded off with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: cekitānas tataḥ khaḍgaṃ kośād uddhṛtya bhārata lāghavaṃ param āsthāya gautamaṃ samupādravat
english: Then Cekitāna, drawing his sword from its sheath, O descendant of Bharata, and assuming the utmost nimbleness, rushed upon Gautama.

sanskrit: gautamo 'pi dhanus tyaktvā pragṛhyāsiṃ susaṃśitam vegena mahatā rājaṃś cekitānam upādravat
english: Gautama too, casting aside his bow and seizing a well-whetted sword, charged with great speed upon Cekitāna, O king.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau balasaṃpannau nistriṃśavaradhāriṇau nistriṃśābhyāṃ sutīkṣṇābhyām anyonyaṃ saṃtatakṣatuḥ
english: Both of them, endowed with strength and bearing excellent swords, hewed at each other with their keen-edged blades.

sanskrit: nistriṃśavegābhihatau tatas tau puruṣarṣabhau dharaṇīṃ samanuprāptau sarvabhūtaniṣevitām mūrchayābhiparītāṅgau vyāyāmena ca mohitau
english: Then those two bulls among men, struck by the force of each other's swords, sank to the earth that bears all creatures, their limbs overcome by a swoon and dazed by exertion.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyadhāvad vegena karakarṣaḥ suhṛt tayā cekitānaṃ tathābhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā samaradurmadam ratham āropayac cainaṃ sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Then Karakarṣa, a friend, ran swiftly forward; seeing Cekitāna, that warrior fierce in battle, in such a plight, he lifted him onto his chariot while all the army looked on.

sanskrit: tathaiva śakuniḥ śūraḥ syālas tava viśāṃ pate āropayad rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ gautamaṃ rathināṃ varam
english: In the same way the valiant Śakuni, your brother-in-law, O lord of peoples, swiftly lifted Gautama, foremost of chariot-warriors, onto his chariot.

sanskrit: saumadattiṃ tathā kruddho dhṛṣṭaketur mahābalaḥ navatyā sāyakaiḥ kṣipraṃ rājan vivyādha vakṣasi
english: And the mighty Dhṛṣṭaketu, enraged, swiftly pierced the son of Somadatta in the breast with ninety arrows, O king.

sanskrit: saumadattir uraḥsthais tair bhṛśaṃ bāṇair aśobhata madhyaṃdine mahārāja raśmibhis tapano yathā
english: The son of Somadatta, with those arrows lodged thickly in his chest, shone forth, O great king, like the sun at midday with its rays.

sanskrit: bhūriśravās tu samare dhṛṣṭaketuṃ mahāratham hatasūtahayaṃ cakre virathaṃ sāyakottamaiḥ
english: But Bhūriśravas in battle, with his excellent arrows, deprived the great chariot-warrior Dhṛṣṭaketu of his chariot, slaying his driver and his horses.

sanskrit: virathaṃ cainam ālokya hatāśvaṃ hatasārathim mahatā śaravarṣeṇa chādayām āsa saṃyuge
english: And seeing him bereft of his chariot, his horses and charioteer slain, he covered him with a mighty shower of arrows in the battle.

sanskrit: sa ca taṃ ratham utsṛjya dhṛṣṭaketur mahāmanāḥ āruroha tato yānaṃ śatānīkasya māriṣa
english: And the high-minded Dhṛṣṭaketu, abandoning that chariot, then mounted the car of Śatānīka, O sire.

sanskrit: citraseno vikarṇaś ca rājan durmarṣaṇas tathā rathino hemasaṃnāhāḥ saubhadram abhidudruvuḥ
english: Citrasena and Vikarṇa, O king, and Durmarṣaṇa likewise, chariot-warriors clad in golden mail, rushed upon the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: abhimanyos tatas tais tu ghoraṃ yuddham avartata śarīrasya yathā rājan vātapittakaphais tribhiḥ
english: Then a terrible battle ensued between Abhimanyu and those three, O king, as of the body assailed by the three humors, wind, bile, and phlegm.

sanskrit: virathāṃs tava putrāṃs tu kṛtvā rājan mahāhave na jaghāna naravyāghraḥ smaran bhīmavacas tadā
english: Though he stripped your sons of their chariots in that great fight, O king, that tiger among men did not slay them, remembering then the words of Bhīma.

sanskrit: tato rājñāṃ bahuśatair gajāśvarathayāyibhiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ samare bhīṣmaṃ devair api durāsadam
english: Then, surrounded by many hundreds of kings mounted on elephants, horses, and chariots, Bhīṣma, hard for even the gods to approach in battle,

sanskrit: prayāntaṃ śīghram udvīkṣya paritrātuṃ sutāṃs tava abhimanyuṃ samuddiśya bālam ekaṃ mahāratham vāsudevam uvācedaṃ kaunteyaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ
english: Seeing him advancing swiftly to rescue your sons, and marking Abhimanyu, that lone youthful great chariot-warrior, the son of Kuntī of the white steeds spoke thus to Vāsudeva:

sanskrit: codayāśvān hṛṣīkeśa yatraite bahulā rathāḥ ete hi bahavaḥ śūrāḥ kṛtāstrā yuddhadurmadāḥ yathā na hanyur naḥ senāṃ tathā mādhava codaya
english: 'Urge on the horses, Hṛṣīkeśa, to where these chariots throng; for these many heroes, skilled in arms and frenzied for battle, must not destroy our army; drive there, O Mādhava.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa vārṣṇeyaḥ kaunteyenāmitaujasā rathaṃ śvetahayair yuktaṃ preṣayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Thus addressed by the son of Kuntī of measureless might, that scion of the Vṛṣṇis sent the chariot yoked with white horses into the battle.

sanskrit: niṣṭānako mahān āsīt tava sainyasya māriṣa yad arjuno raṇe kruddhaḥ saṃyātas tāvakān prati
english: A great uproar arose among your troops, O sire, when Arjuna, enraged in battle, advanced against your men.

sanskrit: samāsādya tu kaunteyo rājñas tān bhīṣmarakṣiṇaḥ suśarmāṇam atho rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Coming upon those kings who guarded Bhīṣma, the son of Kuntī then spoke this word to Suśarman, O king:

sanskrit: jānāmi tvāṃ yudhi śreṣṭham atyantaṃ pūrvavairiṇam paryāyasyādya saṃprāptaṃ phalaṃ paśya sudāruṇam adya te darśayiṣyāmi pūrvapretān pitāmahān
english: 'I know you to be a foremost warrior and my bitter enemy of old; behold now the dreadful fruit of your turn that has come due. This day I shall show you your forefathers long departed.'

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃjalpatas tasya bībhatsoḥ śatrughātinaḥ śrutvāpi paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ suśarmā rathayūthapaḥ na cainam abravīt kiṃ cic chubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
english: Though he heard the harsh speech of Bībhatsu, the slayer of foes, as he spoke thus, Suśarman, that leader of chariot-bands, answered him nothing at all, neither fair nor foul.

sanskrit: abhi gatvārjunaṃ vīraṃ rājabhir bahubhir vṛtaḥ purastāt pṛṣṭhataś caiva pārśvataś caiva sarvataḥ
english: Surrounded by many kings, he advanced upon the hero Arjuna from the front, from the rear, from the flanks, from every side.

sanskrit: parivāryārjunaṃ saṃkhye tava putraiḥ sahānagha śaraiḥ saṃchādayām āsa meghair iva divākaram
english: Encircling Arjuna in battle together with your sons, O sinless one, he covered him with arrows as the clouds cover the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛttaḥ sumahān saṃgrāmaḥ śoṇitodakaḥ tāvakānāṃ ca samare pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: Then there began a most mighty battle, with blood for its waters, between your men and the Pāṇḍavas in the fray, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa tudyamānas tu śarair dhanaṃjayaḥ; padā hato nāga iva śvasan balī bāṇena bāṇena mahārathānāṃ; ciccheda cāpāni raṇe prasahya
english: Saṃjaya said: But Dhanaṃjaya, being smitten by their arrows, hissing like a strong serpent struck by a foot, with arrow after arrow forcibly cut asunder in battle the bows of those great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: saṃchidya cāpāni ca tāni rājñāṃ; teṣāṃ raṇe vīryavatāṃ kṣaṇena vivyādha bāṇair yugapan mahātmā; niḥśeṣatāṃ teṣv atha manyamānaḥ
english: Having shattered in an instant the bows of those valiant kings in battle, the great-souled one pierced them all at once with his arrows, resolving then to leave none of them remaining.

sanskrit: nipetur ājau rudhirapradigdhās; te tāḍitāḥ śakrasutena rājan vibhinnagātrāḥ patitottamāṅgā; gatāsavaś chinnatanutrakāyāḥ
english: Smeared with blood, they fell in the fight, struck down by the son of Indra, O king, their limbs riven, their heads fallen, their lives departed, their armored bodies cut through.

sanskrit: mahīṃ gatāḥ pārthabalābhibhūtā; vicitrarūpā yugapad vineśuḥ dṛṣṭvā hatāṃs tān yudhi rājaputrāṃs; trigartarājaḥ prayayau kṣaṇena
english: Overpowered by Pārtha's might, they fell to the earth and, of varied form, perished all together; seeing those princes slain in battle, the king of the Trigartas rushed forward in an instant.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ rathānām atha pṛṣṭhagopā; dvātriṃśad anye 'byapatanta pārtham tathaiva te saṃparivārya pārthaṃ; vikṛṣya cāpāni mahāravāṇi avīvṛṣan bāṇamahaughavṛṣṭyā; yathā giriṃ toyadharā jalaughaiḥ
english: Then the thirty-two others who guarded the rear of those chariots fell upon Pārtha; surrounding Pārtha and drawing their loud-twanging bows, they rained upon him a great flood of arrows, as the rain-clouds drench a mountain with their torrents of water.

sanskrit: saṃpīḍyamānas tu śaraughavṛṣṭyā; dhanaṃjayas tān yudhi jātaroṣaḥ ṣaṣṭyā śaraiḥ saṃyati tailadhautair; jaghāna tān apy atha pṛṣṭhagopān
english: Hard pressed by that downpour of arrow-floods, Dhanaṃjaya, his wrath kindled in the fight, with sixty oil-washed arrows in the combat slew those rear-guards as well.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ rathāṃs tān avajitya saṃkhye; dhanaṃjayaḥ prītamanā yaśasvī athātvarad bhīṣmavadhāya jiṣṇur; balāni rājñāṃ samare nihatya
english: Having vanquished those sixty chariots in battle, the glorious Dhanaṃjaya, glad at heart, the ever-victorious one, then hastened to slay Bhīṣma, having struck down the forces of the kings in the fray.

sanskrit: trigartarājo nihatān samīkṣya; mahārathāṃs tān atha bandhuvargān raṇe puraskṛtya narādhipāṃs tāñ; jagāma pārthaṃ tvarito vadhāya
english: The king of the Trigartas, seeing those great chariot-warriors of his kinsmen slain, set those lords of men before him in battle and rushed swiftly to slay Pārtha.

sanskrit: abhidrutaṃ cāstrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ vīkṣya śikhaṇḍimukhyāḥ abhyudyayus te śitaśastrahastā; rirakṣiṣanto ratham arjunasya
english: Seeing Dhanaṃjaya, foremost of wielders of weapons, thus assailed, the warriors led by Śikhaṇḍin advanced, keen weapons in hand, eager to guard the chariot of Arjuna.

sanskrit: pārtho 'pi tān āpatataḥ samīkṣya; trigartarājñā sahitān nṛvīrān vidhvaṃsayitvā samare dhanuṣmān; gāṇḍīvamuktair niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ bhīṣmaṃ yiyāsur yudhi saṃdadarśa; duryodhanaṃ saindhavādīṃś ca rājñaḥ
english: And Pārtha, the great bowman, seeing those heroes among men charging together with the king of the Trigartas, scattered them in battle with sharp shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva; and as he sought to reach Bhīṣma in the fight, he beheld Duryodhana and the king of the Sindhus and other kings.

sanskrit: āvārayiṣṇūn abhisaṃprayāya; muhūrtam āyodhya balena vīraḥ utsṛjya rājānam anantavīryo; jayadrathādīṃś ca nṛpān mahaujāḥ yayau tato bhīmabalo manasvī; gāṅgeyam ājau śaracāpapāṇiḥ
english: Advancing against those who sought to bar his way, the hero of boundless valor fought them awhile with his strength; then, leaving aside the king and Jayadratha and the other lords, that mighty-armed, high-spirited one, of fearsome strength, went on, bow and arrows in hand, toward the son of Gaṅgā in the fray.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraś cograbalo mahātmā; samāyayau tvarito jātakopaḥ madrādhipaṃ samabhityajya saṃkhye; svabhāgam āptaṃ tam anantakīrtiḥ sārdhaṃ sa mādrīsutabhīmasenair; bhīṣmaṃ yayau śāṃtanavaṃ raṇāya
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira of terrible might, the great-souled one of endless fame, his anger kindled, came swiftly forward; leaving aside in battle the lord of the Madras, his own appointed share, he went together with the sons of Mādrī and Bhīmasena against Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, for combat.

sanskrit: taiḥ saṃprayuktaḥ sa mahārathāgryair; gaṅgāsutaḥ samare citrayodhī na vivyathe śāṃtanavo mahātmā; samāgataiḥ pāṇḍusutaiḥ samastaiḥ
english: Engaged by those foremost of great chariot-warriors in battle, the son of Gaṅgā, that wondrous fighter, the great-souled son of Śaṃtanu, was not shaken by all the assembled sons of Pāṇḍu come upon him.

sanskrit: athaitya rājā yudhi satyasaṃdho; jayadratho 'tyugrabalo manasvī ciccheda cāpāni mahārathānāṃ; prasahya teṣāṃ dhanuṣā vareṇa
english: Then king Jayadratha, true to his word, of most fierce might and high spirit, coming up in the fight, with his excellent bow forcibly cut asunder the bows of those great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhīmasenaṃ yamau ca; pārthaṃ tathā yudhi saṃjātakopaḥ duryodhanaḥ krodhaviṣo mahātmā; jaghāna bāṇair analaprakāśaiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīmasena, the twins, and Pārtha likewise, the great-souled Duryodhana, his wrath roused in the fight and his fury like venom, struck with arrows bright as fire.

sanskrit: kṛpeṇa śalyena śalena caiva; tathā vibho citrasenena cājau viddhāḥ śarais te 'tivivṛddhakopair; devā yathā daityagaṇaiḥ sametaiḥ
english: By Kṛpa, by Śalya, and by Śala, and likewise, O lord, by Citrasena in the battle, they were pierced with arrows by those whose wrath was greatly swollen, as the gods are by the assembled hosts of the Daityas.

sanskrit: chinnāyudhaṃ śāṃtanavena rājā; śikhaṇḍinaṃ prekṣya ca jātakopaḥ ajātaśatruḥ samare mahātmā; śikhaṇḍinaṃ kruddha uvāca vākyam
english: Seeing Śikhaṇḍin, his weapon cut away by the son of Śaṃtanu, the king Ajātaśatru, the great-souled one, his anger kindled in battle, spoke wrathfully these words to Śikhaṇḍin:

sanskrit: uktvā tathā tvaṃ pitur agrato mām; ahaṃ haniṣyāmi mahāvrataṃ tam bhīṣmaṃ śaraughair vimalārkavarṇaiḥ; satyaṃ vadāmīti kṛtā pratijñā
english: 'Having spoken thus before your father to me, that you would slay that Bhīṣma of the great vow with floods of arrows bright as the spotless sun, you made the vow, saying, "I speak the truth."

sanskrit: tvayā na caināṃ saphalāṃ karoṣi; devavrataṃ yan na nihaṃsi yuddhe mithyāpratijño bhava mā nṛvīra; rakṣasva dharmaṃ ca kulaṃ yaśaś ca
english: 'Yet you do not make that vow bear fruit, in that you do not slay Devavrata in the fight; do not become false to your pledge, O hero among men; guard your duty, your lineage, and your fame.'

sanskrit: prekṣasva bhīṣmaṃ yudhi bhīmavegaṃ; sarvāṃs tapantaṃ mama sainyasaṃghān śaraughajālair atitigmatejaiḥ; kālaṃ yathā mṛtyukṛtaṃ kṣaṇena
english: 'Behold Bhīṣma in the fight, of terrible swiftness, scorching all the hosts of my army with nets of arrow-floods of exceeding fierce splendor, like Death wrought by Time in an instant.'

sanskrit: nikṛttacāpaḥ samarānapekṣaḥ; parājitaḥ śāṃtanavena rājñā vihāya bandhūn atha sodarāṃś ca; kva yāsyase nānurūpaṃ tavedam
english: 'Your bow cut away, heedless of the battle, vanquished by the son of Śaṃtanu, the kingly one, abandoning your kinsmen and your brothers, whither will you go? This is not worthy of you.'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā hi bhīṣmaṃ tam anantavīryaṃ; bhagnaṃ ca sainyaṃ dravamāṇam evam bhīto 'si nūnaṃ drupadasya putra; tathā hi te mukhavarṇo 'prahṛṣṭaḥ
english: 'For seeing that Bhīṣma of boundless valor, and our army broken and fleeing thus, you are surely afraid, O son of Drupada; for the color of your face is downcast.'

sanskrit: ājñāyamāne 'pi dhanaṃjayena; mahāhave saṃprasakte nṛvīra kathaṃ hi bhīṣmāt prathitaḥ pṛthivyāṃ; bhayaṃ tvam adya prakaroṣi vīra
english: 'Even while Dhanaṃjaya joins this great battle, O hero among men, how is it, O renowned upon the earth, that you this day show fear of Bhīṣma, O hero?'

sanskrit: sa dharmarājasya vaco niśamya; rūkṣākṣaraṃ vipralāpānubaddham pratyādeśaṃ manyamāno mahātmā; pratatvare bhīṣmavadhāya rājan
english: Hearing the harsh-syllabled speech of the King of Righteousness, bound up with rebuke, that great-souled one, taking it as a command of censure, hastened to the slaying of Bhīṣma, O king.
